overview: Click service logs click_id + ad_id to Kafka and 302-redirects. Flink dedups by click_id, aggregates in 1-min tumbling windows with watermarks for late events, and writes to an OLAP store (ClickHouse/Pinot) with idempotent upserts. Raw clicks also land in S3; a nightly Spark job recomputes for billing reconciliation.

estimation.assumption: Illustrative ingest: 100K clicks/s at 100 B per event.
estimation.result: A one-minute batch contains around 6M events before deduplication.
estimation.implication: Partition ingestion, retain raw events and materialize small window aggregates for queries.

entityDetails.purpose: Immutable source events retained for replay and billing reconciliation.
accessPatterns: Append an accepted click; replay an event-time range.
constraints: Dedup click_id within a defined retention window; validate redirects and never count a retried click twice.

accessPatterns: Upsert one ad/minute aggregate; query an advertiser time range.
constraints: Use idempotent window/version upserts; define watermarks and corrections for late data.

apiDetails.purpose: Record a click and redirect to the verified advertiser URL.
apiDetails.rationale: Acknowledge/log durably before counting; duplicate click IDs do not produce duplicate billable events.
Expose the aggregation freshness and late-event correction policy; operational totals and settled billing can differ.

failureCases.scenario: Late or duplicate events change a previously shown count
failureCases.handling: Dedup by click_id, use event-time windows and publish corrected aggregate versions. Reconcile billing from raw events with a documented cutoff.

alternatives: Use windowed streaming for low-latency aggregates and explicit late-event handling. Use micro-batches when minute-level freshness is sufficient and simpler bounded-input processing outweighs the latency floor. Both retain raw events and reconcile billing.
